# `parts.import`

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs-gen` from crates/ew-commands/schemas/parts.import.schema.json. Do not edit: change the source and regenerate. -->

`parts.import` (`ImportParts`, FT-410): creates project-local part copies, the one command that does (a copy of
another library is embedded with `library.embed`, which refuses project-local items), with the project-local
manufacturer copies the parts name (WP-S1.19 D10).

`copies` holds part and manufacturer copies in the `lib/` JSON form (doc 05 §3.4), as a parts table import
produces them: the shell and `ew import parts` read the file and parse it (`ew_import_tables::parse_parts_tables`,
the golden dialect), the command never sees a path. At least one part copy. Each copy is checked, at `/copies/i`:
- it reads as a library document of kind `part` or `manufacturer` (else invalid);
- its `id` is the copy identity `v5(NS_LIBCOPY, library_id ‖ item_id)` and its `sha256` the hash of its item
  (the rules of `library.embed`);
- its `library_id` is the project's ID: the copy is project-local;
- a part copy has a `key` (`meta.key`), which is what a re-import matches on; a key or a copy listed twice is
  invalid.

**Duplicates.** A part copy whose key a project-local part copy of the project has already, or whose copy ID
exists, is skipped and counted; nothing is updated (updating a part is FR-PRT-014's previewed command). The rest
are inserted in the given order, in one transaction (one undo step). A manufacturer copy is inserted only when an
inserted part copy names it (its `library_id` and `item_id` are the part's `manufacturer` reference) and its copy
ID does not exist yet, so no manufacturer copy is left without a part; when every part copy is skipped the
transaction is empty.

Cost `Bulk` (always previewed: the shell shows the card with the created and skipped counts), exposure `Edit` (the
GUI, `ew import parts`, and a command log replayed by `ew apply`). Outcome: the first inserted part copy; the note
`created <n>, skipped <m>`, which counts the part copies.

## Exit codes

A command runs as one line of a command log replayed by `ew apply` ([doc 17 §3.5](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#35-command-logs-ewcmd)). The exit code of `ew apply` is:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The line committed as one transaction. |
| 1 | A prevent rule or the command's own domain rule refused the line (`Prevented`, `Rejected`); without `--one-step` the lines before it stay committed and are saved, with `--one-step` nothing is saved. |
| 2 | Anything else stops the replay: invalid parameters, a missing record, an unresolvable reference, an open, lock or save error. |

The codes of every subcommand are in [doc 17 §3.2](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#32-exit-codes).

This is a bulk command: a log line runs it as a preview first and commits the previewed result ([doc 17 §3.5](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#35-command-logs-ewcmd)).
